findings.evidence: The only "write" allowed is persisting an in-context document to disk verbatim so you can `Read` it.
findings.fix: Delete this persist allowance: Phase 1 step 1 (lines 28-31) already mandates a hard STOP with 'input not on disk' when the caller passed inline content, so the two branches give opposite answers for the same input; keep the caller-must-persist rule as the only path.

findings.evidence: Description names WHAT/WHEN/keywords but never states the audit-only boundary, so near-miss fixer queries ('review and fix my design spec in a loop') cannot be excluded from the description alone.
findings.fix: Replace the description with: 'Framework-aware checklist reviewer for spec-driven-development documents — classifies each document into one of four archetypes (intent, requirements, design, plan) and reviews it with the matching checklist plus the source framework's own conventions (EARS, RFC-2119 SHALL, Given/When/Then, OpenSpec delta sections, Spec Kit [NEEDS CLARIFICATION]/[P], constitutional gates). Audit only: reports severity-rated findings, never edits the document or applies fixes — fixing is ai-kit-spec-review-fixer's job. Use when a design, spec, requirements, or plan document has been produced and needs review before the next step; not for code/PR review, linting, or drafting specs and plans. Works on superpowers, OpenSpec, GitHub Spec Kit, Kiro, BMAD, GSD, or generic (docs/rfcs, docs/designs). Accepts a pre-resolved FRAMEWORK_PROFILE_PATH + ARCHETYPE from the orchestrator; falls back to its own framework detection + archetype heuristics when none provided.'

findings.evidence: Prefer targeted reads (line ranges, codegraph_explore queries, rg matches) over reading whole files when only one section is needed.
findings.fix: Scope the targeted-reads advice to exploration only and exempt factual-claim verification: the codebase-grounding rule (lines 201-204) requires reading the referenced file's content to confirm a claim, and a one-section targeted read can false-confirm a claim contradicted elsewhere in the file — say 'for claim verification, read the whole referenced file'.

findings.evidence: For a `fused` doc the orchestrator may pass several archetypes — apply each one's checklist.
findings.fix: Require each finding on a fused document to name the archetype whose checklist produced it (e.g. prefix the title with '[design]'), so the orchestrator can route findings per archetype via the profile's revise_protocol routes without inferring from Location.

findings.evidence: ### Cross-Document Consistency appears only when two or more files were reviewed — but no rule says what to check or write under it.
findings.fix: Add one line defining the check: contradictions between reviewed files (spec vs plan, design vs requirements) in the same finding shape, and that a single-file review never emits the heading.

findings.evidence: Three phases: (1) resolve framework + archetype (below), (2) apply the matching archetype checklist(s)…
findings.fix: Delete the Workflow section (lines 20-24); the Phase 1/2/3 headings immediately below already carry the same sequence verbatim.
